hero.title: Someone to think out loud with.
hero.subtitle: Makker is a chat on top of language models that stay in the EU or on your own server. Write, attach a document, pick a role, and get the answer as text, Word or PowerPoint. Open source, with a filter that stops personal data before it leaves the browser.
hero.trust: AGPL-3.0 · Passkeys and two-factor login · Export your data with one click

values.aiTitle: Think out loud with a model
values.aiBody: Write the way you talk. Attach minutes or a draft, pick a role — sparring partner, devil's advocate, plain-language editor — and get an answer that stays. The model runs at Mistral in the EU or locally with Ollama.
values.dataBody: Your conversations are yours: only you can see them, and you can take them out as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click. The workspace can be deleted completely again.
values.securityBody: Workspaces are separated in the database, not just in the code. Passkeys, two-factor login and a log that cannot be edited.

family.body: Makker is one tool in the Haij family of open source tools for organisations that want to own their own technology.

demo.title: Try it without creating anything
demo.body: You get your own workspace with roles and tasks ready to use. It is deleted after {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}. No email, no sign-up.
demo.privacy: Do not put real personal data in the demo. It passes through a database and possibly a language model on the way.

dataExport.title: Data and export
dataExport.subtitle: Take a complete copy of everything this workspace holds.
dataExport.xlsxBody: One file with a tab per kind of data. For you, or for anyone who needs to look without knowing Makker.
dataExport.jsonBody: The same data as JSON with every id kept, so you can move to something other than Makker without losing the links between conversations, messages and files.
dataExport.sheetsLabel: Tabs in the file (named in Danish, as the file writes them):
dataExport.notBackupBody: An export can be read but not restored, and it is only as fresh as the day you downloaded it. The night's encrypted dump is what saves you when the database is gone.
dataExport.privacy: The export contains your own conversations, messages and files, the workspace's roles and tasks, and its history. Other people's conversations are never included, not for the owner either. Passwords, passkeys and the key to the workspace's language model are never included. Downloading it is recorded in the audit log.

ai.setupIntro: Makker is a chat and cannot answer without a model. Set one up:
ai.setupOutro: Then start Makker again. Without a model the writing field says so, and settings, roles and tasks can still be edited.
ai.limitsHint: A model call costs money on a hosted installation and minutes on a local one. The numbers are generous for a person and mean for a script.
ai.messageLength: Characters in a message, at most
ai.principleDecides: The AI answers, the person decides. The model writes an answer; it never sends anything out of the house, never deletes anything and changes nothing unless you do.
ai.principleUndo: Every conversation is your own. You can delete it, and you can take it out.
ai.principleData: What you write, and what your documents contain, is sent to the model as data, never as instructions. The system prompt and the roles live on the server, where the administrator sets them.
ai.principleSovereign: The model can be swapped, including for a local one. Who can see what is listed in docs/subprocessors.md.
ai.testPatience: A local model may have to be read off disk first. That can take up to a minute the first time.
ai.failAuth: The key was rejected. Check the workspace's own key below, or the installation's MISTRAL_API_KEY.
ai.failUnreachable: Nothing is listening at that address. Is Ollama running? Check OLLAMA_BASE_URL.
ai.failConfig: The model is set up wrong. Correct the model name below, or LLM_MODEL in .env.
ai.failGeneric: The call failed. The details are below and in the server log.
ai.failRateLimited: Mistral refused the call as too many (429). The key works, but the account or plan sets the ceiling: on the free Experiment plan this happens often when the model is busy, and a key under a workspace with no active plan gets the same answer. Check Billing and Limits on console.mistral.ai for the organisation the key belongs to.
ai.failWhereToLook: The details are in the server log.
ai.testNotAllowed: Only the owner or an administrator can test the connection.
ai.withoutBody: Makker is built around the conversation: without a model you can still see your conversations, take them out and edit the workspace's roles and tasks, but the writing field says so plainly, and nothing breaks.
ai.perInstallation: Calls across the installation per day
ai.failCeiling: Makker's own ceiling on AI calls was reached, not the provider's. The ceilings are under “Ceiling on AI calls” below; the installation's own is set with AI_DAILY_CALL_CAP. Try again shortly.

terms.title: Terms and privacy
terms.intro: Makker is an open source tool for thinking out loud with a language model, run by Haij. This is the agreement between you and us when you use the edition we run. If you run the code yourself, only the licence applies.

what.title: What Makker is
what.body: A chat on top of a language model: you write, attach documents, pick a role, and get answers as text or as a Word or PowerPoint file. We make no promise that the answers are right; read them as a draft from a colleague, not as the verdict.

account.title: Accounts and access
account.body: You get in by applying or being invited. We store your name, your email and your workspace's name, and use them to sign you in and to write to you about the service. Passwords are stored hashed, and you can add a passkey and two-factor. We sell nothing, and we do not send marketing you did not ask for.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.body: Everything you write in Makker belongs to you and your workspace. Only you can see your conversations; they can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click and deleted again. We do not look at them unless you ask us for help, and we never pass them on.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: With a language model set up, what you write, the contents of the documents you attach, the workspace's system prompt and the role you chose are sent to the model provider. Who that is stands under Settings → AI and in the list of subprocessors. The personal-data filter runs in your browser before anything is sent.

leaving.title: Leaving
leaving.body: You can delete your workspace immediately, without writing to anyone and without waiting. The export is one click away and readable without Makker. We keep no copy afterwards beyond the nightly encrypted backups, which roll off after 30 days — on the server and in the EU storage they are copied to.

availability.title: Running and guarantees
availability.body: Makker is new, and there is no uptime guarantee. We look after your data with encrypted backups every night, but take an export now and then if your conversations matter. The service is provided as it is, without warranties beyond what the law requires.

license.title: Licence
license.body: The code is AGPL-3.0. You may use it, change it and run it yourself; if you change it and offer it to others over a network, your changes must be available too. What you write in the tool is not covered by the licence — that is yours.

demo.title: The demo
demo.body: A demo workspace is created without e-mail or sign-up and deleted entirely after 24 hours, account included. Do not put real personal data in it. We keep only the technical log data needed to keep the demo running.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to martin@vintherconsulting.dk. If you have found a security problem, SECURITY.md in the repository says how to report it; use that rather than an ordinary email.

help.title: Help
help.intro: How Makker works, in the order you meet it.

chat.title: The conversation
chat.body: Write the way you talk, and the answer arrives as it is written. Every conversation is your own: nobody else in the workspace can see it, not the owner either. Start as many as you like, name them and delete them again.

roles.title: Roles
roles.body: A role is laid over the workspace's system prompt for one conversation: sparring partner, devil's advocate, critical reader, plain-language editor, careful reader or teacher. It does not replace the prompt, so the language and the frame still hold. The administrator can edit the roles and make new ones.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: The task library is ready-made tasks you can click: answer an enquiry, summarise the document, challenge my plan. The text lands in the writing field, and the role switches with it when the task has one that fits.

files.title: Files
files.body: Attach PDF, Word, text or Markdown. The text is pulled out once at upload and goes into the conversation, so the model can read it. The file stays in your conversation and travels with the export.

export.title: Word and PowerPoint
export.body: Ask for a memo or a deck, and download the answer as a Word or PowerPoint file in Haij's template. The model delivers the content; the template shapes it. Two sharply separated steps, so the look is always the same.

pii.title: The filter
pii.body: Before anything is sent, the browser looks for personal data: national ID numbers, account numbers, addresses, and words that point at health, finances or criminal cases. It warns, and it blocks what must not be sent. Everything happens locally; nothing leaves the machine to be checked.

ai.title: What the AI may do
ai.body: The model answers, you decide. It never sends anything out of the house, never deletes anything and changes nothing unless you do. What you write and what your documents contain is treated as data, never as instructions.

data.title: Your data
data.body: Your conversations can be taken out as a spreadsheet and JSON under Settings → Data. The workspace can be deleted completely again, audit trail included.

pii.title: The message looks like it contains personal data.
pii.softTitle: The message may mention sensitive information.
pii.disable: Switch the filter off for this conversation
pii.off: The filter is off for this conversation.
pii.note: The filter recognises known formats — national ID, e-mail, account and card numbers, diagnosis codes — and a few fixed phrases like “my name is”. It cannot catch names, addresses or health written freely in prose, it does not look inside attached files, and it knows nothing of your legal basis. A reminder, not a guarantee.
pii.softNote: The filter cannot see the information itself — only that the words appear.

explain.health: Health is a special category under GDPR article 9 and needs a stricter basis than ordinary data.
explain.union: Trade union membership is a special category under article 9 too.
